newsitem.title: USA: US June jobless statistically significant-Abraham.
newsitem.headline: US June jobless statistically significant-Abraham.

text.p: Bureau of Labor Statistics Commissioner Katharine Abraham said Thursday the rise in the June jobless rate was statistically significant but its implications for the economy remained unclear.
"It's statistically significant but I'm not sure how economically meaningful it was," Abraham said.
The jobless rate in June rose to 5.0 percent from May's 4.8 percent.
Abraham said she would not describe the rise in the jobless rate as a "blip" but said it was important to see next month's data. "We want to see what next month's data brings."
Abraham also said her department would be working on ways to improve seasonaly adjustment of local government employment data.
Local government payrolls jumped 78,000 in June after a 6,000 drop in May. The Labor Department said it had problems adjusting those figures for the end of the school year.
